explanations.explanation: That's the greeting Jesus gets, friend. Matthew 8:28 says He "…was met by two demon-possessed men coming from the tombs." Two of them, and not one is holding a welcome sign.

Nice guess, but the text never mentions fishermen here. It says He "…was met by two demon-possessed men coming from the tombs." (Matthew 8:28). A crowd of fishermen would have been a calmer day for everybody.

A group of tax collectors isn't who meets Him on this shore. Here it's "…two demon-possessed men coming from the tombs." (Matthew 8:28). Two men, not a group with clipboards. Honestly, the clipboards might have been less scary.
Yep, the tombs. Matthew 8:28 says the two men came "…from the tombs." That's a place with burial graves, and nobody goes there for a picnic. When somebody walks out of there toward you, you notice.

A synagogue is where people gather to worship, and that's not where these men come from. The text says they were "…coming from the tombs." (Matthew 8:28). Tombs and a synagogue are very different neighborhoods, friend.
The marketplace isn't the place the text names, baker. Matthew 8:28 says the men came "…from the tombs." The same verse adds that they were so violent no one could pass that way.

That's the word, baker. Matthew 8:28 says they were "…so violent that no one could pass that way." Think of a road that everybody just agrees to skip. When the whole route gets cancelled because of two men, that's serious.

Sick is a fair thought, and I bet these men were hurting. But the word the text uses is violent. They were "…so violent that no one could pass that way." (Matthew 8:28). I think that detail tells you how much people stayed away.

Unclean is a word you hear a lot in the Bible, so I get why it came to mind. It's not the word here, though. Matthew 8:28 says they were "…so violent that no one could pass that way." The text is talking about how dangerous the road was.
True, and that's the surprise. They shout, "What do You want with us, Son of God?" (Matthew 8:29). They call Jesus the Son of God to His face. I'd say they knew exactly who He was.

It's actually true. The two men shout, "What do You want with us, Son of God?" (Matthew 8:29). Calling Him the Son of God means they knew exactly who He was. It's a wild thing to hear from men coming out of the tombs.

explanations.answer: Torture them before the appointed time
explanations.explanation: That's the exact question. They ask, "Have You come here to torture us before the appointed time?" (Matthew 8:29). The text doesn't say what the appointed time is, so I'll leave that one alone too. What I can say is that they were asking Jesus a question, and they shouted it.

explanations.answer: Send them back across the sea
explanations.explanation: Not quite, baker. Nothing in the passage mentions sending them back across the sea. They ask whether He has come "…to torture us before the appointed time?" (Matthew 8:29). The sea does come back later in this story, just in a very different way.

explanations.answer: Bring the whole town against them
explanations.explanation: That's not what they ask. The town doesn't even enter the story until later, in Matthew 8:33-34. Here they shout, "Have You come here to torture us before the appointed time?" (Matthew 8:29).

Not this time, friend. The demons beg for a favor, and Jesus answers with one word: "Go!" (Matthew 8:32). No speech, no warm-up, no three points and a closing story. I could learn something here, because I can't say hello in under a paragraph.

Right, no long speech. After the demons ask to be sent into the pigs, Jesus says one word: "Go!" (Matthew 8:32). That's it. I wish I could be that short when somebody asks me where I put the sprinkles.

explanations.answer: Down the steep bank into the sea
explanations.explanation: Yes, down the steep bank and into the sea. Matthew 8:32 says "…the whole herd rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters." Notice that it says the whole herd. Not one pig hung back to check the weather.

explanations.answer: Off the road and into the town
explanations.explanation: The herd doesn't head for town, baker. The town hears about it later from the men tending the pigs (Matthew 8:33). The herd itself "…rushed down the steep bank into the sea…" (Matthew 8:32).

explanations.answer: Back across the hills to the tombs
explanations.explanation: Not back to the tombs, friend. Matthew 8:32 says they "…rushed down the steep bank into the sea and died in the waters." The pigs had been feeding in the distance (Matthew 8:30), but the text sends the whole herd down the bank into the sea.

Not quite, friend. Matthew 8:33 says they reported "…all this, including the account of the demon-possessed men." So they told about the pigs and about the two men. That's the whole story, not just the part with the herd.

That's right, it's false. The text says they reported "…all this, including the account of the demon-possessed men." (Matthew 8:33). So the herd was only part of the news. I think that was a lot to say in one breath after running into town.

That's the one, baker. Matthew 8:34 says that when they saw Him, "…they begged Him to leave their region." The whole town came out, and that was their request. The text doesn't tell us why, so I'll stay out of their heads.
Bless would have been a nice ending, but that's not what happens. Matthew 8:34 says they "…begged Him to leave their region." The text doesn't give a reason, so I won't make one up.
They don't ask Him to visit, friend. It's the opposite. Matthew 8:34 says the whole town "…begged Him to leave their region." The whole town did come out to meet Him, but that's what they asked.
